title: Not Waiting for Miracles: Mary & Lydia's 25-Year Fight for Financial Independence
excerpt: Mary learned tailoring in the 90s, ran a village kiosk, baked cakes, made detergents and soaps, hustled in Nairobi for 8 years. Lydia ran an M-PESA agent and barbershop. Every venture collapsed—not from lack of effort, but from predatory loans, exploitative villagers, medical emergencies eating capital, and a system designed to fail disabled entrepreneurs.
author: AbleHearts Team
content:
# Not Waiting for Miracles: Mary & Lydia's 25-Year Entrepreneurial Fight **They are NOT sitting around waiting for handouts. They've been fighting for financial independence for over 25 years.** Mary has tried **6 different businesses**. Lydia managed **2 businesses** despite immobility. Every single one collapsed—**not from laziness, but from systemic exploitation, predatory microfinance, medical crises, and a village economy designed to crush the vulnerable.** This is their untold entrepreneurial story. --- ## ✂️ Late 1990s: Mary Learns Tailoring—Her First Dream ### The Breakthrough: Against All Odds **Late 1990s (before the 21st century):** - 🎓 **Mary enrolls in a tailoring course** at a local training institute (Nyanchwa Technical and Vocational Training Centre) - ♿ **Despite physical mobility challenges**, she masters the skills - ✂️ **She gets a sewing machine**—her first business tool - 🌟 **Hope is alive:** "I can work. I can earn. I can support my family." ### The Harsh Reality: Village Business = Exploitation **Why the tailoring business failed:** #### 1. **"We Raised You" Entitlement Culture** - 👗 Villagers place orders but never pay - 💬 **"We're neighbors, you can wait"** - 💬 **"We helped your family, now you owe us"** - 💬 **"You're disabled, you should be grateful we're 'supporting' your business"** **Result:** Mary works for free, making clothes she never gets paid for. #### 2. **"Who Pays a Disabled Woman?" Discrimination** - 🚫 Customers refuse to pay full price - 💬 **"You're slow because of your legs, why should I pay full price?"** - 💬 **"Other tailors are faster, I'll pay you half"** - ♿ **Disability = Discount in villagers' minds** **Result:** Even when paid, it's below cost—unsustainable. #### 3. **Cannot Follow Up for Payments** - 🦽 **Mary's mobility is limited**—she can't chase debtors door-to-door - 🏚️ Villagers know she can't "follow up" like able-bodied tailors - 💸 **Debt accumulates, no enforcement possible** **Result:** She's left with unpaid invoices, no legal recourse. #### 4. **High Material Costs, Zero ROI** - 🧵 Purchasing fabric and thread costs money upfront - 📉 **Returns on Investment (ROI): ZERO** - 💔 She's working at a loss, depleting savings **Final Outcome:** > **Tailoring career dies in early 2000s. But Mary never loses hope.** --- ## 🏪 2000s: Village Kiosk—Selling Fast-Moving Goods ### The Pivot: Small-Scale Retail **Mary opens a village kiosk (small shop):** - 🛒 **Sells fast-moving goods:** sugar, soap, flour, kerosene, sweets - 🏡 **Typical village setting:** Small wooden structure, basic inventory - 💪 **Mary manages it despite limited mobility** ### The Trap: Predatory Microfinance (KWFT Loan) **Around 2010:** - 💰 **Mary takes a loan from KWFT (Kenya Women Finance Trust)**—a microfinance institution - 🎯 **Purpose:** Boost the kiosk business, buy more inventory - 📈 **Hope:** Expand the business, increase profits **The Loan Terms (Predatory):** - 📊 **Interest rates: RIDICULOUS** (often 20-40% annual in Kenyan microfinance) - ⏳ **Short repayment period** (weekly/monthly payments, no grace for emergencies) - 📜 **Fine print villagers can't read**—Mary's mother signed papers she didn't fully understand - 🚫 **No regulation:** Local government fails to protect vulnerable borrowers ### The Collapse: The Cow Is Repossessed **What happened:** - 📉 **Business profits can't cover loan repayments** (interest too high) - 🩺 **Medical emergencies drain capital** (Mary's health issues, family needs) - 💸 **KWFT demands repayment** - 🐄 **KWFT repossesses the family's ONLY milking cow** instead of working out a payment plan **The Cow = Family Lifeline:** - 🥛 **Daily milk for nutrition** - 💰 **Selling milk = income** - 👨‍👩‍👧 **Symbol of family security** ### The Suicide Attempt: Breaking Point **When the cow was taken:** - 😭 **Mary's mother (now deceased, 2019 poisoning) attempts suicide** - 🌊 **She goes to the river to drown herself** - 🆘 **Villagers intercept and save her** - 💔 **But the cow never comes back** **This is the reality of predatory microfinance in Kenya:** > Local government fails to regulate. Villagers sign papers they can't read. Microfinancers take EVERYTHING—even the family's survival assets. **Final Outcome:** > **Kiosk business collapses. Family deeper in poverty. But Mary keeps fighting.** --- ## 🍰 2010s: Baking, Detergents, Soaps—Hands-On Skills ### The Comeback: Community-Based Entrepreneurship **Mary learns new skills through DETERMINATION:** #### 1. **Baking Local Cakes** - 🎂 **Weddings, birthdays, local events** - 🍞 **Traditional Kenyan cakes, mandazis, chapatis** - 👰 **Villagers order for celebrations** #### 2. **Making Detergents** - 🧪 **Mixing reagents and water** - 🧴 **Selling locally-made laundry soap** - ♻️ **Affordable for villagers (cheaper than store-bought)** #### 3. **Making Bar Soaps** - 🧼 **Handmade soaps for washing** - 🌿 **Using local ingredients** ### The Vision: Empowering Other Disabled People **Mary's dream:** - 🤝 **Recruit other disabled people in the village** - 📚 **Teach them these skills** - 💪 **Create a cooperative of disabled entrepreneurs** - 🌍 **Achieve financial independence together** **Why this made sense:** - 🏘️ **Village life doesn't require huge capital** - 👥 **Community-based support network** - 🛠️ **Hands-on skills = sustainable income** ### The Death: Same Pattern, Different Business **Why this venture also failed:** 1. **Same "We Know Each Other" Exploitation** - 💬 **"We're villagemates, I'll pay next month"** - 📉 Never pays 2. **Medical Emergencies Drain Capital** - 🩺 Mary's health issues - 💊 Medication costs - 🏥 Hospital visits - **Every medical crisis = business capital gone** 3. **Unstable Village Economy** - 📉 Villagers themselves are poor—can't consistently buy - 🌧️ **Drought years = no income for anyone** - 💸 **No cash flow = business dies** **Final Outcome:** > **Baking/detergent/soap business dies. But Mary STILL doesn't give up.** --- ## 🏙️ 2012-2020: Nairobi Hustle—City Survival ### The Move: Trying the Capital City **2012:** - 🚌 **Mary moves to Nairobi** (Kenya's capital) - 🎯 **Goal:** Find "manageable hustles" to support herself and her 2 school-going kids - 🏢 **City = More opportunities** (she hopes) **What she did in Nairobi:** - 🛒 **Informal sector work** (selling goods, small-scale trading) - 🧹 **Any work she could manage** with limited mobility - 👧 **Supported by her firstborn daughter** (who acted as caregiver) **Who was left behind:** - 🏡 **Lydia stayed in the village** (with Mary's mother as caregiver) - 👧 **The orphaned girl (Mary's sister's child)** also in the village ### 2019: The Poisoning—Everything Falls Apart **Refer to [Mary & Lydia's Story](/blog/mary-lydia-story-20-years-resilience-disability-kenya):** - ☠️ **2 family members poisoned, Mary's mother (the caregiver), Mary's sister** - 😭 **Both Mary's mother & Mary's sister dies, 2 weeks apart, same hospital** - 🏚️ **Housing crisis intensify** (threats of land grabbing) - 💔 **Lydia now has no caregiver** **Impact on Mary's Nairobi life:** - 🚫 **Cannot stay in Nairobi without a caregiver** - 💸 **Hiring a caregiver in Nairobi = UNAFFORDABLE** - 👧 **Lydia and the orphaned girl need care too** - 🧮 **Math doesn't work:** Mary needs a caregiver + Lydia needs a caregiver + child needs care = IMPOSSIBLE ### 2020: COVID-19—Forced Return to Village **March 2020:** - 🦠 **COVID-19 lockdowns** - 🏙️ **Nairobi becomes UNBEARABLE** (no work, no income, high cost of living) - 🚌 **Mary returns to the village** - 🏡 **Mary + Lydia reunite in the village** (cheaper to survive together) - 👧 **Firstborn daughter stays in Nairobi to hustle** **But Nairobi isn't kind to the daughter either:** - 💼 **Multiple sudden layoffs** - 📉 **Unstable gig economy** - 😰 **She's struggling too** **Why we focus on Mary, Lydia, and the child:** > They are the most urgent in need. The daughter is trying to survive herself. **Final Outcome:** > **Mary's 8-year Nairobi hustle ends. Back to village poverty. But she's STILL fighting.** --- ## 🏦 Lydia's Story: M-PESA Agent & Barbershop Receptionist ### Education Denied: The Exam Registration Scandal **Lydia's background:** - 🎓 **Studied under Kenya's 8-4-4 education system** - 📚 **Completed 8 years of primary school** - 🧠 **Smart, capable, eager to learn** **But:** - 🚫 **The school REFUSED to register her for national exams (KCPE)** - 💬 **School's reason:** _"We don't want bad grades. You'll tarnish our reputation."_ - 📊 **Schools are ranked by exam scores**—disabled students are seen as "liabilities" **Result:** - 🎓 **No primary school certificate** - 🚫 **Cannot pursue secondary education or vocational training** (certificate required) - 💔 **Lydia becomes a DROPOUT—not by choice, but by discrimination** **If you think this is rare in Kenya:** > This is systematic. Disabled students are routinely denied exam registration to protect school rankings. ### No Tech Access = No Online Opportunities **Why Lydia stayed stuck:** - 🌐 **No internet in the village** (until now, we're raising funds for Starlink) - 💻 **No computer or smartphone** - 📚 **No access to online courses, remote work, tech skills** **If she had tech access in 2010:** - 👩‍💻 She could have learned coding, design, virtual assistance - 🌍 She could have worked remotely for global clients - 💰 She could have earned USD/EUR income from Kenya **But without access:** > She was trapped in the village with zero opportunities. ### The Businesses: M-PESA Agent & Barbershop Receptionist **What Lydia did:** #### 1. **M-PESA Mobile Money Agent** - 📱 **M-PESA = Kenya's mobile money system** (send/receive money via phone) - 🏪 **Lydia ran a small M-PESA agent kiosk** - 💵 **Villagers come to deposit, withdraw, send money** - 🧍‍♀️ **Perfect for Lydia:** Standing job, no need to walk around **Why it worked (briefly):** - 📍 **She stood at the kiosk all day** (immobility not a barrier) - 💰 **Earned commission on transactions** - 👥 **Helped the community with financial services** #### 2. **Kinyozi (Barbershop) Receptionist** - ✂️ **Kinyozi = Local barbershop** - 🧍‍♀️ **Lydia stood at reception**, took payments, managed appointments - 💇 **Again, standing job suited her limitations** ### Why Both Businesses Collapsed **1. Medical Emergencies "Eat" All Capital** - 🩹 **Lydia's 10+ year untreated leg wounds** flare up - 🏥 **Emergency hospital visits** - 💊 **Medication costs** - 💸 **All business capital goes to medical bills** **The Cycle:** 1. ✅ Build business capital ($50-100) 2. 🩺 Medical emergency hits 3. 💸 Capital = $0 4. 🔄 Take loan, crowdfund, start from ZERO 5. 📉 Repeat forever (rat race never ends) **2. "Living Healthy Is a Blessing"** - 🏥 **Disability = Unpredictable medical costs** - 💰 **No insurance, no savings** - 🚑 **Every emergency = bankruptcy** **3. Unstable Village Economy** - 📉 **Villagers themselves are poor** - 💸 **Low transaction volumes** (M-PESA commissions = pennies) - 🌧️ **Drought years = zero business** **4. Poor Management? Or Impossible Circumstances?** > **"Maybe someone can say this lacks good management for the business but be in their 'shoes'"** **From their perspective:** - 🏚️ **Surviving in a collapsing house** (housing crisis ongoing) - 🩺 **Medical emergencies every few months** - 💸 **No safety net, no insurance** - 🌍 **No access to global markets** (no internet until now) > **It's NOT poor management. It's IMPOSSIBLE circumstances.** **Final Outcome:** > **M-PESA business: Dead. Barbershop job: Gone. But Lydia still has hope.** --- ## 💔 The Pattern: Why Every Business Failed ### It's NOT Laziness. It's SYSTEMIC BARRIERS.
| **Barrier** | **Impact** | |-------------|-----------| | **Predatory Microfinance** | KWFT took the family cow, crushing future business attempts | | **Exploitative Villagers** | "We raised you" = free labor, no payment | | **Disability Discrimination** | "Who pays a disabled woman?" = below-cost pricing | | **Medical Emergencies** | Every health crisis drains ALL business capital | | **No Legal Recourse** | Can't follow up on debts, can't sue, can't enforce | | **Unstable Economy** | Village poverty = no consistent customers | | **No Internet/Tech Access** | Trapped in local economy, no global opportunities | | **School Discrimination** | Lydia denied exams = no certificate = no formal opportunities |
### The Math Never Works **For a stable business, you need:** 1. ✅ Consistent customers 2. ✅ Fair pricing 3. ✅ Legal enforcement of payments 4. ✅ Financial safety net for emergencies 5. ✅ Access to markets (physical or digital) **What Mary & Lydia have:** 1. ❌ Exploitative customers who don't pay 2. ❌ Forced discounts because of disability 3. ❌ No legal recourse (can't chase debtors) 4. ❌ Medical emergencies wipe out capital 5. ❌ No internet = trapped in village economy > **Even with perfect management, these barriers make success IMPOSSIBLE.** --- ## 🌟 They're Not Begging. They're Asking for a BRIDGE. ### What They've Proven **Mary's track record:** - ✅ Learned tailoring (1990s) - ✅ Ran a kiosk (2000s) - ✅ Took entrepreneurial risk (KWFT loan, even though it backfired) - ✅ Learned baking, detergents, soaps (2010s) - ✅ Recruited other disabled people to empower them - ✅ Hustled in Nairobi for 8 years (2012-2020) - ✅ Supported 2 children through school (one finished, one struggling) **Lydia's track record:** - ✅ Overcame school discrimination (denied exams) - ✅ Ran M-PESA agent business - ✅ Worked as barbershop receptionist - ✅ Stood 12-16 hours/day despite immobility and leg wounds - ✅ Helped community with financial services ### What They're Asking For **NOT handouts. A BRIDGE to opportunity:** #### 1. **Starlink Internet** ($600 kit + $120/month) - 🌐 **Access to global online work** (transcription, VA, customer service) - 🎓 **Free online courses** (coding, design, AI tools) - 🩺 **Telemedicine** (consult doctors remotely) - 📺 **Mental health therapy** (YouTube, educational content) #### 2. **Tech Skills Training** (from [Tech Education Facility](/blog/ablehearts-tech-education-facility-empower-people-with-disabilities-digital-skills)) - ��‍💻 **Coding, graphic design, AI prompting** - 💰 **Earn USD/EUR remotely** (escape village poverty) - 🌍 **Work for global clients** #### 3. **Adaptive Technology** (from [China Adaptive Furniture](/blog/china-adaptive-furniture-tech-solutions-disabled-kenya)) - 🪑 **Standing-support chair** (Lydia can work comfortably) - ⚡ **Solar power** (reliable electricity for online work) - 🏠 **Smart home tech** (voice control = independence) #### 4. **Stable Housing** ([Permanent Housing Fund](/donate)) - 🏡 **End the housing crisis** (no more eviction threats) - 🧠 **Mental stability** (trauma recovery requires safety) - 🏢 **Workspace for online work** (stable internet, desk, chair) --- ## 🚀 Through Tech & AI, They Can Have a Better Living ### The Global Remote Work Revolution **What's possible NOW (2025) that wasn't possible in 2010:**
| **2010 (When Lydia Was Denied Opportunities)** | **2025 (If She Gets Internet + Skills)** | |-----------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------| | ❌ No internet in village | ✅ Starlink = 100 Mbps anywhere | | ❌ No online courses | ✅ Free courses (Coursera, YouTube, freeCodeCamp) | | ❌ No remote work | ✅ Upwork, Fiverr, Toptal (earn $10-50/hour USD) | | ❌ No AI tools | ✅ ChatGPT, Midjourney, Canva (AI-powered work) | | ❌ Trapped in village economy | ✅ Global clients pay in USD/EUR |
### Real Income Potential **If Lydia learns:** - 💻 **Virtual Assistant:** $10-20/hour = $800-1,600/month - 🎨 **Graphic Design:** $15-40/hour = $1,200-3,200/month - 👩‍💻 **Basic Coding:** $20-50/hour = $1,600-4,000/month - 🤖 **AI Prompt Engineering:** $25-60/hour = $2,000-4,800/month **Compare to:** - 🏚️ **Village kiosk:** $20-50/month (before medical emergencies eat it) - 📱 **M-PESA agent:** $10-30/month commission > **Online work = 20-100X village income. But ONLY with internet + skills.** --- ## 🤝 Only With Your Support ### This Is NOT a Handout.
